title: Quality control and the quality register
blurb: Describe quality control, what the quality register records, who uses it, and how its records feed stage and project reports.
question: A product fails an inspection, but the team expects it to pass after a small fix. What does PRINCE2 say about repeating the check and recording it?

teach.body: Formally: quality control is the set of procedures that monitor specific products and their development or delivery activities to find out whether they comply with relevant standards, and to identify ways to minimize causes of unsatisfactory performance. In plain English: check each product against its quality specifications as it is made, record what happened, and learn how to stop the same faults recurring.

steps.label: Obtain approval
steps.sub: as named in the product description

teach.caption: The methods, responsibilities and standards come from the product descriptions and the quality management approach.

teach.h: What a quality register entry shows
head: Heading
Example entry
rows: Reviewer: R. Shah; approver: senior user
Fail; retest after fix booked 9 May
teach.caption: The register records the activity and its result (typically pass or fail) and the response if the product fails.

teach.body: The quality register summarizes all quality management activities that are planned or have taken place. The project manager and project assurance use it when reviewing progress: are planned checks happening on time, and are products passing? It is part of the project log, set up in initiation. Its format and that of other quality records is set in the standards section of the quality management approach.

teach.caption: If a product fails but is expected to pass, it may be reasonable to repeat the quality control activity.

items.label: Quality register set up in the project log
Team manager updates it as checks are done
PM confirms required approvals on receipt
Checked; feeds the end stage report
Checked, feeds the end project report, closed

teach.h: Worked scenario: a ferry terminal kiosk
teach.body: At Harbourgate Ferries, team manager Nia Pryce's team builds self-service ticket kiosks. Each kiosk's product description names a usability trial and an electrical safety inspection, with the operations lead as approver. One kiosk fails the safety inspection over a loose earth lead; Nia records the fail, the team fixes it, the repeat inspection passes, and both results go in the quality register. Project manager Leila Haddad checks the register before accepting the completed work package, and later uses it in the end stage report.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) The quality register records quality activities and their results; the PRODUCT register lists all products of a plan and their status. (2) The register merely records the activity and result; it does not set quality specifications. (3) Quality control is done within the project; quality assurance is the independent check that those controls are appropriate.

items: Quality control monitors products against standards and looks for ways to reduce poor performance.
Carry out quality methods; record activity and result in the quality register.
Register headings: quality method, dates, responsibilities, result.
Used by the PM and project assurance to review progress.
A failed check may be repeated if a pass is expected.
Register information feeds end stage reports and the end project report.

summary: You can now describe quality control, list what the quality register records, and say who uses it. You can also trace how quality records flow into end stage and end project reports, and how a failed check is handled.

A.q: What is the purpose of the quality register?
options: To list all products required of a plan and their status
To summarize all quality activities planned or performed
To describe the quality standards the project will follow
To record the user's quality expectations and criteria
A.why: The quality register summarizes all quality management activities that are planned or have occurred; the PM and project assurance use it to review progress (manual 8.5).

whyNot.0: Listing products and their status is the purpose of the product register.
whyNot.2: Standards are described in the quality management approach.
whyNot.3: Expectations and acceptance criteria are in the project product description.

A.q: Which information typically appears in a quality register entry?
options: Benefit, measure, baseline and owner
Purpose, composition, derivation, format and quality specifications
Cause, event, effect and proximity
Quality method, dates, responsibilities and result
A.why: Quality register entries show the quality method, planned and actual dates, responsibilities, and the result with any response to failure.

whyNot.0: These describe benefits tracking in the benefits management approach.
whyNot.2: These describe a risk in the risk register.

A.q: Which roles use the quality register as part of reviewing progress?
options: The project manager and project assurance
The business layer and the executive
The senior supplier and quality assurance
The change authority and the senior user
A.why: The quality register is used by the project manager and project assurance as part of reviewing progress (manual 8.5).

whyNot.1: The business layer and executive receive reports rather than reviewing the register.
whyNot.2: Quality assurance is independent of the project; the register is a project tool.
whyNot.3: The change authority decides on changes, and the senior user represents users on the board; neither is named as reviewing progress through the register.

B.q: A product fails an inspection, and the team expects it to pass after a minor fix. What is appropriate?
options: Remove the failed entry from the quality register
Raise an exception report to the project board
Repeat the check and record both results
Mark the product as passed with a note
B.why: If a product fails a quality control activity and is expected to pass, it may be reasonable to repeat the activity; the register records each activity and result (manual 8.3.1.2).

whyNot.0: The register is a record of activities and results; a failed result stays recorded.
whyNot.1: An exception report is for a forecast breach of stage or project tolerance, not a single failed check.
whyNot.3: A product that has not passed cannot be recorded as passed.

B.q:
Which two statements about quality control are correct?
1. It monitors products to see whether they comply with standards.
2. It is performed independently of the project management team.
3. It seeks ways to minimize causes of unsatisfactory performance.
4. It sets the quality tolerances for each product.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Quality control monitors products and their delivery activities against standards (1) and identifies ways to minimize causes of unsatisfactory performance (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 describes quality assurance, not quality control.
whyNot.2: Both are false: independence describes quality assurance, and tolerances are set in quality planning.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: tolerances are set in quality planning.

B.q: Which reports draw on the information in the quality register?
options: End stage reports and the end project report
Issue reports and exception reports
The project brief and the project mandate
Work package descriptions and team plans
B.why: Quality control activities recorded in the quality register provide information for end stage reports and the end project report (manual 8.3.1.2).

whyNot.1: Issue and exception reports describe issues and forecast tolerance breaches, not quality records.
whyNot.2: The mandate and brief exist before initiation, before any quality control takes place.
whyNot.3: Work package descriptions and team plans are planning products that come before the checks.

C.q: In managing product delivery, who updates the quality register, and whom do they notify of completed quality activities?
options: The project manager; the project board
Project assurance; the senior user
The team manager; the project manager
The senior supplier; the executive
C.why: When executing a work package, the team manager notifies the project manager of completed quality activities and updates the quality register (manual 17.4.2).

whyNot.0: Managing product delivery is the team manager's process; the board is not involved in it.
whyNot.1: Project assurance reviews the register; it does not carry out the delivery work.
whyNot.3: The senior supplier sits on the board and is not involved in executing work packages.

C.q: When receiving a completed work package, what should the project manager confirm, and where are the approvers defined?
options: Each product's requisite approval; its product description
Each product's actual cost; the quality management approach
Each product's risk owner; the risk register
Each product's benefit; the business case
C.why: The PM ensures each product in the work package has gained its requisite approval, as defined in the quality and sustainability responsibilities in its product description (manual 16.4.3).

whyNot.1: The QMA sets general responsibilities and standards; approvers for a product are in its product description.
whyNot.2: Risk owners relate to risks, not product approval.
whyNot.3: Benefits are tracked through the business case and benefits management approach, not product receipt.

C.q: Where is the format of the quality register and other quality records set, and in which process is the register closed?
options: Product description; managing a stage boundary
Quality management approach; closing a project
Project product description; initiating a project
Quality register itself; controlling a stage
C.why: The standards heading of the quality management approach covers the composition and format of the quality register and other quality records; the register is checked and closed in closing a project.

whyNot.0: A product description covers one product; the register is checked at a stage boundary but closed in closing a project.
whyNot.2: The PPD holds expectations and acceptance criteria; initiation is when the register is set up.
whyNot.3: The register does not define its own format, and it stays open through controlling a stage.

reteach.title: An MOT logbook
reteach.question: How do you prove a car was checked properly?

blocks.body: At an MOT the tester follows set checks (the method), records the date, who tested and the result. If the car fails on a bulb, it is fixed and retested, and both results are on record. Later anyone can look back and see what was checked and when. The quality register works the same way for project products, and its records feed the stage and project reports.

blocks.text: The logbook records checks; it does not decide what standard the car must meet. That lives in the specification.

explain.body: Quality control checks products and their delivery activities against standards and looks for ways to reduce poor performance.

test.q: Which element of quality management monitors specific products against relevant standards?
options: Quality planning
Quality assurance
Project assurance
Quality control
test.why: Quality control is the procedures that monitor specific products and their development or delivery activities against relevant standards.

whyNot.0: Quality planning sets specifications and produces product descriptions and the QMA.
whyNot.1: Quality assurance gives independent confidence that the controls are appropriate.
whyNot.2: Project assurance checks for the board that the project is run correctly.

explain.body: The quality register records each quality activity and its result, typically pass or fail.

test.q: Where is the result of a product test recorded?
options: Product register
Quality register
Issue register
Daily log
test.why: Quality control activities and their results are recorded in the quality register.

whyNot.0: The product register lists products and their status, not test results.
whyNot.2: The issue register holds formal issues.
whyNot.3: The daily log holds informal issues and notes.

explain.body: The PM and project assurance use the register to see whether planned checks are happening and products are passing.

test.q: Why does the quality register show both planned and actual dates?
options: To set the stage's time tolerance
To calculate the risk budget
To help review quality progress
To schedule post-project reviews
test.why: The register summarizes activities planned or performed so the PM and project assurance can review progress.

whyNot.0: Stage time tolerance is set by the project board.
whyNot.1: The risk budget funds risk responses.
whyNot.3: Post-project reviews are planned in the benefits management approach.

explain.body: Register information is used in end stage reports and the end project report, and the register is closed in closing a project.

test.q: In which process is the quality register closed?
options: Managing a stage boundary
Controlling a stage
Directing a project
Closing a project
test.why: In closing a project the quality register is checked to confirm the final stage's quality activities were performed, feeds the end project report, and is closed.

whyNot.0: At a stage boundary the register is checked for the stage, not closed.
whyNot.1: The register is used throughout controlling a stage.
whyNot.2: Directing a project is the board's process; it does not maintain the register.
